Title: Systemic failures and insider threats: Reassessing airport security
Article:
THE article by Sharanjit Singh in NST yesterday (Aug 11, 2026) is commendable for its insightful and timely examination of Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) security issues.
The author demonstrates a strong grasp of both policy and criminological dimensions, offering a nuanced and well-reasoned perspective that goes beyond surface-level commentary.
Such thoughtful analysis contributes meaningfully to public discourse on national security and border management in Malaysia.
The concerns surrounding security at KLIA deserve to be examined beyond the immediate question of whether airport scanners are sufficiently modern or whether individual officers have performed their duties properly.
The more fundamental criminological question is: how can criminal actors exploit a highly regulated environment that is specifically designed to prevent such activities?
The answer may lie in understanding airport security as a system of guardianship, opportunity and institutional integrity, rather than simply a technological exercise.
From a criminological perspective, crime occurs not only because motivated offenders exist, but also because opportunities arise when capable guardianship is inadequate.
KLIA is an extraordinarily complex environment involving immigration, aviation security, customs, airport operators, airlines, ground handlers, auxiliary police and other personnel. The larger and more complex the system becomes, the greater the possibility of gaps between agencies, responsibilities and lines of accountability.
Therefore, when prohibited items pass through an international airport, the question should not simply be, "Why did the scanner fail?" It should also be, "At which point did the security chain fail?"
This distinction is important. Technology is only one component of security. A sophisticated scanner operated inadequately, interpreted incorrectly or placed within a weak overall security architecture does not necessarily produce effective security.
Recent government comments that existing scanners are capable of detecting contraband, while screening priorities have traditionally focused more heavily on weapons and explosives, reinforce the need to examine the entire security model rather than immediately assuming that equipment is the principal problem.
The second issue is insider vulnerability. Airports are unusual criminogenic environments because thousands of employees legitimately possess varying degrees of access to restricted areas, baggage systems, aircraft and operational information.
[[nid:1509489]]
This creates what criminologists would describe as an insider-threat problem. An employee does not necessarily have to be corrupt from the beginning. Recruitment by criminal networks can occur through financial incentives, coercion, personal relationships or gradual involvement.
Consequently, security vetting cannot be regarded as a one-off exercise conducted when a person is recruited. For particularly sensitive positions, there must be continuing risk assessment, appropriate monitoring and mechanisms for identifying unexplained behavioural or financial indicators.
Third, authorities should consider whether individual incidents represent isolated offending or manifestations of established criminal networks.
If the same route, airport facility, employee category or method repeatedly appears in different cases, investigators should look for patterns rather than treating every incident as an independent event.
This is where intelligence-led policing becomes critical.
Enforcement agencies should be asking not merely who carried the prohibited item, but who recruited that person, who financed the activity, who facilitated access, who expected the shipment and whether the same network has used other couriers or routes.
Fourth, there is an important issue of organisational accountability. When security fails, responsibility can easily become fragmented.
One agency may blame equipment, another manpower, another procedures and another individual misconduct. Such fragmentation can create what criminologists call an accountability gap.
A serious post-incident review should therefore reconstruct the entire security chain and identify precisely where preventive, detective and supervisory controls failed.
Finally, KLIA should be viewed not merely as an airport but as Malaysia's primary international border gateway. Repeated security breaches have implications extending beyond drug trafficking or contraband.
They potentially affect public confidence, Malaysia's international reputation and the credibility of the country's border-management system.
The lesson, therefore, is not simply that KLIA needs better machines. It needs a layered security architecture combining technology, competent personnel, intelligence, inter-agency information sharing, continuous integrity management and independent accountability.
The most important question is consequently not only "Who failed?" but "What allowed the failure to occur, remain undetected and potentially be exploited?"
That is the criminological question that deserves much greater attention.
* The writer is a criminologist at the Centre for Policy Research, Universiti Sains Malaysia

Title: Woman charged with operating RM1.7mil kootu scheme
Article:
ALOR STAR: A woman was charged in the Sessions Court today with organising a tontine (kootu) scheme involving more than RM1.7 million since last year.
Siti Zulaika Ahmad Sabri, 36, pleaded guilty after the charge was read before judge Sharmila Abdul Samad.
According to the charge, she organised the scheme involving 52 participants who made cash payments into the fund between July 2025 and July this year at a house in Kampung Padang Satu, Bukit Kayu Hitam, Changlun.
The charge under Section 3 of the Kootu Funds (Prohibition) Act 1971 carries a maximum fine of RM500,000, a prison sentence of up to 10 years, or both, upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutors Muhammad Fahmi Kamaluddin and Vatchira Wong Rui Fern urged the court to set bail at RM100,000, citing the accused's financial capacity and potential flight risk.
The accused, who was unrepresented, did not make any plea regarding the bail offer.
Sharmila denied bail and fixed Sept 22 for facts of the case and sentencing. The accused will be held at Pokok Sena Prison pending proceedings.
On Aug 4, it was reported that a couple and their son from Taman Desa Bayanmas, Bukit Kayu Hitam, were reported missing on July 20 over debts linked to the scheme.
Two days later, the woman and a 39-year-old man
surrendered
at the Kubang Pasu police station at 1.50am.

Title: Johor to cancel housing approvals if developers delay affordable homes
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Johor will cancel housing project approvals if developers fail to meet agreed deadlines for their affordable housing commitments.
Johor Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said affordable housing components must not lag behind open-market developments.
He said commitments to provide Rumah Mampu Milik Johor (RMMJ) units were an obligation to the people, rather than merely figures on development plans.
He said this yesterday after chairing the third 2026 meeting of the Housing Planning, Evaluation and Design Committee (PDRC), attended by representatives from the state Housing Development Corporation (PKPJ), State Secretary's Office, Land and Mines Office, local authorities and other agencies.
"Developers cannot push ahead with open-market projects while delaying RMMJ units for lower- and middle-income households.
"Open-market housing and RMMJ must move in tandem. We do not want the commercial component to move far ahead while affordable housing continues to be delayed," he said.
The committee has held 37 PDRC sessions covering all 10 districts, 16 local authorities, 152 developers and 190 projects, involving a combined commitment of 45,575 housing units targeted for completion by 2030.
The latest meeting reviewed proposed developments in Johor Baru, Kulai and Mersing, including layout changes, the provision and relocation of RMMJ units and compliance with the state's affordable housing policy.
Jafni said one application required 394 RMMJ units to be built first as the open-market component had already begun.
"An RMMJ commitment is a trust and responsibility to the people, not merely a figure on a development plan.
"The timeline must be clear, compliance monitored and follow-up action taken firmly.
"Developers were also required to complete applications with the relevant agencies within the agreed period. Failure to meet the deadline could result in the approval being cancelled," he said.
Jafni said developers would be closely monitored to ensure their commitments translated into construction and, ultimately, keys being handed to buyers.
He said the PDRC would also scrutinise facilities, including mosques, multipurpose halls, kindergartens, gated areas and guardhouses, to ensure RMMJ developments provided a safe and liveable environment.
"Affordable housing is not merely about four walls and a roof. Homes must have good access, a safe environment, adequate community facilities and prices that reflect people's affordability," he said.
Jafni said incentives for buyers, including air-conditioning units, kitchen cabinets and access facilities, had also been retained for developments in Bandar Baru Permas Jaya.
He said Johor was targeting 30,000 RMMJ units for B40 and M40 households by the end of 2026, followed by 100,000 units by 2030.
"What has been approved must be implemented, what has been promised must be delivered, and what is the people's right must be defended," he said.

Title: Customs foils bid to hide RM650,000 worth of cannabis in rubbish heap
Article:
KANGAR: A drug syndicate's attempt to hide a sack containing more than 8kg of cannabis in a rubbish heap was foiled by the Perlis Customs Department.
Perlis Customs director Mohammad Furiman Hattar said the seizure of 8.123kg of cannabis flowers, worth RM649,840, was among six enforcement operations conducted by the department this year.
He said the drugs were seized at about 11.50am on May 21 after a Perlis Customs Narcotics Unit team spotted a suspicious white sack behind a stall while patrolling Lembah Chuping, Padang Besar.
"The syndicate's modus operandi was to leave the drug-filled sack in a rubbish heap to evade detection, assuming enforcement personnel would not inspect it.
"However, the team's diligence thwarted the attempt," he told a press conference at the Perlis Customs Department office here today.
He said the Kuala Perlis Marine Enforcement Branch also foiled an attempt to smuggle 17 compressed cannabis slabs weighing 17kg and worth RM51,000, after they were found on a platform at Pulau Batu Layang on June 19.
"Both cases are being investigated under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952," he said.
Furiman said the department also foiled four other smuggling attempts involving cigarettes, gas stoves and liquor.
He said the total value of seizures, including duties and taxes, from all six cases was estimated at RM1.77 million.
For cigarettes, he said 82,960 sticks of various brands suspected to be uncustomed were seized in two separate operations — a raid at a house in Jitra, Kedah, on July 9 and a vehicle inspection in Kuala Perlis on July 23.
The department also seized a container holding 5,840 imported gas stoves worth more than RM300,000, including duty, at North Port, Port Klang, on July 21, after detecting an inaccurate Customs declaration.
In the sixth case, Customs raided an empty warehouse in Taman Industri Bena Jaya, Port Klang, on July 29 and seized 1,016 litres of uncustomed liquor worth more than RM687,000, including taxes.
He said the four cases were being investigated under the Customs Act 1967.

Title: Bangladeshi man charged with murder of three compatriots
Article:
SEREMBAN: A Bangladeshi man was charged at the magistrate's court today with the murder of three male compatriots earlier this month.
Md Idris Ali, 43, nodded to indicate he understood after the charges were read before magistrate Nurul Saqinah Rosli.
However, the magistrate ruled that a foreign language interpreter be called to re-read the charges after observing that the accused had difficulty understanding Bahasa Malaysia.
"All three charges were read to the accused. However, based on the court's observation, the accused did not fully understand them.
"Therefore, the court has fixed Aug 13 for an interpreter to re-read the charges to the accused in a language he understands," she said.
According to the charges, the accused allegedly murdered Md Nozrul Islam, Mohasin, and Kiron Miah.
The offences were committed at a back alley behind a house in Taman Linggi and an oil palm plantation in Sua Manggis, Port Dickson, between 3.30pm and 4pm on Aug 1.
He was charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which carries the death penalty or imprisonment between 30 and 40 years, and up to 12 strokes of the rotan if not sentenced to death.
Meanwhile, at the Sessions Court, the accused faced another charge of attempting to murder Bangladeshi national Md Kajal Mondol in Taman Linggi at 4pm on the same day.
The charge under Section 307 of the Penal Code carries a maximum prison term of 10 years and a fine upon conviction.
Judge Tasnim Abu Bakar postponed reading the charge to Aug 13 to allow an interpreter to present it in a language the accused understands.
State prosecution director Engku Ahmad Rashdi Engku Abdillah offered no bail.

Title: MCBA warns firms over fake procurement documents using DG's identity
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) has warned companies to be wary of fraudulent government procurement documents bearing the signature of its director-general (DG).
The agency said it had received complaints from companies that were sent documents purportedly issued as Letters of Acceptance for government procurement exercises.
The purported procurements involved supplies including tactical protective jackets, generator sets and stationery.
MCBA said the documents were believed to contain forged signatures of its director-general and other officers, as well as fake agency letterheads, to convince companies that the offers were genuine government transactions.
"A police report has been lodged over the misuse of the names of the MCBA director-general and its officers, and the matter has been referred to the authorities for investigation and further action," the agency said in a statement today.
MCBA said that all its procurement matters were conducted in accordance with existing government procurement procedures, regulations and rules.
It advised parties receiving an offer letter or Letter of Acceptance purportedly issued by the agency to verify its authenticity before making any financial commitment.
The agency said it viewed seriously any impersonation, document forgery or misuse of the names, identities and positions of MCBA officers that could damage its reputation.
Members of the public were also advised to remain vigilant to avoid falling victim to similar scams.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police cripple housebreaking syndicate with arrest of five Chinese citizens
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police have crippled a housebreaking syndicate following the arrest of five men from China during two raids in Sri Petaling and Pudu.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the arrests followed investigations into a break-in at a residence in Taman Desa Petaling on Aug 4, where a victim lost cash, jewellery, and a luxury sling bag worth RM6,000.
"Acting on information and intelligence, police carried out two raids in Sri Petaling and Pudu at 9.30pm on Aug 9.
"Police seized a vehicle and various tools believed to have been used to break into houses," he said in a statement today.
Fadil said police also recovered items belonging to the complainant during the raids.
"Other luxury items, including watches and wallets, were also seized, along with more than RM10,000 in cash comprising various foreign currencies.
"Preliminary investigations revealed that the suspects are also believed to be involved in two other housebreaking cases in Cheras," he said.
Fadil added that the five suspects, aged between 38 and 58, have been remanded from Aug 10 to 13 to assist investigations.
The case is being investigated under Section 457 of the Penal Code for housebreaking.

Title: Rosmah must secure RM67.5m or face enforcement, says Global Royalty
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Lebanese jewellery company Global Royalty Trading SAL says its RM67.5 million judgment against Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor remains protected whether she complies with the High Court's condition for a stay pending her appeal or not.
The company's lawyer Datuk David Gurupatham said Rosmah, the wife of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, must deposit the full judgment sum into a joint stakeholder account within 30 days from today to enjoy the stay.
The senior lawyer said the money would remain secured in the account pending the outcome of Rosmah's appeal at the Court of Appeal.
"Should Global Royalty ultimately succeed in the appeal, our client will be able to look to the monies already secured in the stakeholder account towards satisfaction of the judgment, subject to the appropriate orders of court," he said.
He said if Rosmah failed to deposit the full amount within the 30-day period, Global Royalty would be entitled to proceed with execution of the judgment.
"In practical terms, therefore, our client is protected in either event, the full judgment sum is either secured within 30 days, or our client is entitled to proceed with enforcement," he said.
Gurupatham said his client would consider all lawful avenues of enforcement if the condition was not complied with, including enforcement against assets disclosed or identified in materials filed by Rosmah in support of her stay application.
"In support of her stay application, Rosmah placed before the Court her Affidavit in Support relating to assets which she represented as having an estimated value of approximately RM666.739 million," he said.
Earlier, judicial commissioner Marianne Antoinette Ghani
granted Rosmah a conditional stay of execution on a RM67.5 million judgment obtained by Lebanese jewellery company Global Royalty Trading SAL, pending her appeal at the Court of Appeal.
She said the conditional stay was the appropriate solution to balance the rights of both parties, ensuring Global Royalty was assured of the fruits of its successful litigation while protecting Rosmah's right of appeal.
On June 10, a separate High Court ordered Rosmah to pay RM67.5 million to Global Royalty after finding her liable for the loss of 43 pieces of jewellery that had been sent to her on consignment.
Rosmah subsequently filed an appeal and sought a stay of execution pending its disposal. The High Court today granted the stay subject to the deposit condition.
Global Royalty had filed a US$14.57 million suit against Rosmah over the loss of more than 40 pieces of jewellery allegedly loaned to her.

Title: Police seek Indonesian man over Banting plantation murder
Article:
KUALA LANGAT: Police are seeking an Indonesian man believed to have information that could assist investigations into the murder of a 49-year-old man at an oil palm plantation in Banting.
Kuala Langat police chief Superintendent Mohd Akmalrizal Radzi said the man, known as "Balancing", was being sought as a witness in the investigation.
He said police were investigating the case under Section 302 of the Penal Code for
murder
.
The latest development comes after police arrested eight people in connection with the case.
The victim, a 49-year-old local man, was found unconscious at an oil palm plantation in Banting at about 5pm on Aug 9.
Police received a report on the discovery from a policeman attached to the Internal Security and Public Order Division of the Kuala Langat district police headquarters.
Akmalrizal had previously said eight people suspected of involvement in the case were subsequently arrested.
Police also released a photograph of "Balancing" to assist in locating him.
Anyone with information on the man is urged to contact the nearest police station or the Kuala Langat district police headquarters operations room at 03-3187 2222.

Title: Multi-layered security strategy needed for more secure borders
Article:
LETTER:
Recent drug-smuggling cases have shown that criminal networks are becoming more organised, mobile and creative.
They use commercial flights, cargo routes, fishing boats, tankers, hidden road compartments and illegal border crossings.
This threatens public safety, weakens the economy and exposes young people to exploitation.
In February 2026, the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency in Pahang seized 1.572 tonnes of methamphetamine worth an estimated RM83.75 million from two vessels and detained 18 crew members from Thailand and Indonesia.
It was the agency's largest drug seizure in Pahang waters.
In July, police have crippled six trafficking attempts through Kuala Lumpur International Airport and seized 247.8 kilogrammes of cannabis worth about RM19.82 million believed to be intended for Europe and arrested seven suspects.
Other cases show how syndicates recruit vulnerable people. In Johor, also in July, police arrested eight people, including a 16-year-old alleged drug transporter, and seized drugs worth RM3.04 million.
Police also reported that 180 Malaysians had been detained overseas as suspected drug mules between 2024 and April 2026.
Recently, a case involving a Malaysia Airlines pilot smuggling drugs in Indonesia shocked everyone.
To curtail such persistent crimes, the first improvement should be using emerging technology such as AI and a single real-time border intelligence system led by the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS).
Police, Customs, Immigration, maritime enforcement, ports and airports should be able to compare passenger information, cargo declarations, vehicle movements, vessel records and criminal watchlists quickly.
Shared risk alerts would help officers identify suspicious people and shipments earlier while allowing lawful travellers and businesses to move more smoothly.
Second, Malaysia needs layered surveillance instead of depending mainly on fixed checkpoints. Coastal radar, drones, thermal cameras, cargo scanners, detection dogs and mobile patrol teams should be deployed according to risk.
At sea, authorities should examine unusual vessel movements and ships that switch off tracking signals. On land, patrols should change locations and operating hours so that syndicates cannot easily predict them.
New equipment must also come with trained analysts, proper maintenance and functioning command centres.
Third, Malaysia must invest in the officers guarding its borders. AKPS has said it needs 400 investigating officers and a much larger workforce to support its operations.
Personnel should receive joint training in narcotics detection, forged documents, financial investigation, cyber evidence and human-trafficking cases. Integrity is equally important.
High-risk postings should be rotated, protected reporting channels should be available, and corruption allegations must be investigated independently.
Finally, regional cooperation must become faster and more practical. Asean customs authorities have already supported joint operations and information-sharing against illicit drugs and other illegal trade.
Malaysia should promote round-the-clock contact points, shared suspect and vessel alerts, coordinated patrols, joint investigations and quicker action against criminal funds.
Fishermen, transport workers and border communities should also have safe ways to report suspicious activity.
Malaysia cannot stop every crime at its borders, but it can make smuggling far more difficult, costly and risky.
Stronger security requires connected agencies, reliable technology, honest officers and trusted regional partners.
Secure borders should protect legitimate movement while stopping those who abuse it.
DR. G PERIASAMY
Senior research fellow
National Institute of Public Administration (INTAN)
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt urged to let 15th Parliament complete full term
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government has been urged to ensure the 15th Parliament completes its full term until Dec 18 next year, unless it loses the confidence of the House.
It has also been urged to convene a cross-party leaders' summit to agree on a common reform agenda for the remainder of the parliamentary term.
The call was made by a coalition of 44 civil society organisations and 25 people, including Project Stability and Accountability for Malaysia, Angkatan Belia Islam Malaysia, the Coalition for Clean and Fair Elections and the Center to Combat Corruption and Cronyism.
They said the government should allow parliament to complete its full term to realise as many reforms as possible to strengthen democracy and improve good governance.
"Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim should convene a cross-party leaders' summit involving all government and opposition parties represented in parliament to establish a common agenda for the remaining term of the 15th Parliament.
"With credit for realising these reforms shared across parties and MPs, these should include constitutional amendments to introduce the separation of the attorney-general and public prosecutor and impose a 10-year tenure limit for prime ministers," they said in a statement today.
The group said PKR and DAP should use their upcoming congresses and conferences on Aug 15 and 16 to push for reforms needed to ensure opposition parties were treated fairly.
"This is to ensure healthy multiparty competition and avoid a return to the pre-2018 system of one-party dominance," the group said.
They also urged the federal and state governments to responsibly pre-announce their preferred dates for early dissolution if they did not intend to serve their full terms.
They said this would make preparations easier for voters and stakeholders, including the Election Commission, police, civil servants, schools, political parties and private sector operators in the transport, hospitality, food and beverage and printing sectors.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lar gibbon linked to Indian actor Vikram traced to Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A lar gibbon at the centre of an investigation involving Indian actor Vikram has been traced to Malaysia, with records listing the country as its place of origin.
The development comes after a video of Vikram playing with and hugging the gibbon went viral, drawing criticism over the possession and handling of the protected animal.
The Hindu reported that Chennai Wildlife Warden Yogesh Kulal said the gibbon had since been moved to Erode, India, from businessman C.K. Ranganathan's residence in Injambakkam.
Records show that the trail of the lar gibbons can be traced to Erode and, before that, Manipur, with Malaysia listed as their country of origin.
Erode district forest officer K.V. Appala Naidu said two gibbons, a male and a female, were found on Keshavanathan's premises.
He said Keshavanathan had informed authorities that he had applied to keep three gibbons, but one had died earlier.
"We need to verify if the animal actually died or if there was an undocumented transfer," he was quoted as saying.
Sources said Ranganathan was believed to have obtained the animals from Keshavanathan, although the transfer certificate had yet to be approved by the authorities.
Chief Wildlife Warden Rakesh Kumar Dogra said the department was investigating how the animals entered the country and whether all legal requirements governing their possession and transfer had been met.

Title: Wong Chen apologises for quitting early, stands by his 13-year-record
Article:
PUCHONG: Former Subang MP Wong Chen said today he was not apologising for his years of service as an elected representative, but for stepping down a year before the next general election.
"No, I am not apologising for resigning. I'm explaining what drove me to make that decision.
"I have done my job as a diligent MP over the last 13 to 14 years.
"Resigning one year early is the apology I give to the people. I could have waited until Parliament was dissolved, but I chose to step down," he told reporters at the Bersama headquarters here.
Wong said his decision to resign was driven by what he described as a duty to defend democracy and the Federal Constitution.

Title: Situation in West Bank requires urgent action: UN envoy
Article:
NEW YORK: The situation in the West Bank must be treated as an emergency requiring urgent action, said a United Nations (UN) envoy on Tuesday, reported Xinhua.
"The concern is not only the continued expansion of (Israeli) settlements, but the speed and systematic manner in which new facts are being created on the ground," warned the official in a briefing to the Security Council.
Ramiz Alakbarov, the Deputy Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process said new outposts are established, often with state support, and can be retroactively authorised or incorporated into the wider settlement system.
From these outposts, settler violence and intimidation have driven the displacement of Palestinian communities, he added.
The spread of agricultural and grazing outposts is deeply troubling as well. Requiring only a few settlers, they enable control over vast areas of land.
Israeli monitoring organisations report that agricultural and pastoral outposts now exercise effective control over close to 20 per cent of the West Bank, he said.
"We must be clear-eyed about what is taking place. These are interconnected steps, not isolated developments.
"They are reshaping the West Bank, weakening Palestinian governance and advancing de-facto annexation," said the envoy.
The stakes are high. If the West Bank continues to unravel, it will further erode the prospects for ending the Israeli occupation and realising a negotiated Israeli-Palestinian peace based on the two-state solution, he warned.
"We must act now, collectively and determinedly, to ensure concrete steps are taken towards that objective.
"The UN remains committed to supporting all efforts in support of a lasting peace between Israelis and Palestinians based on 1967 lines, with Jerusalem as capital of both States, living side by side in peace and security," he said.
Alakbarov warned that the West Bank is at a breaking point.
He said the situation was not the result of a sudden deterioration, but of decades of unresolved conflict that has deepened the unlawful Israeli occupation, pushed the Palestinian Authority to the brink of collapse, and undermined prospects for an independent, viable and sovereign Palestinian state.
As of Monday, 76 Palestinians have been killed in the West Bank in 2026, including 18 children, by Israeli forces or settlers.
Three Israelis, including one civilian and two members of Israeli security forces, were killed in confrontations with Palestinians in the West Bank, the envoy noted.
Some 127 Palestinian communities have experienced full or partial displacement since January 2023, including 47 that have been entirely displaced, affecting more than 6,390 Palestinians.
In 2026 alone, about 3,800 Palestinians, nearly half of them children, have been displaced due to settler violence, demolitions and evictions, he said.
Settler violence has reached unprecedented levels.
So far this year, the UN has documented more than 1,430 incidents involving Israeli settlers that resulted in casualties, property damage or both, affecting approximately 260 Palestinian communities.
Many incidents occurred in the presence of Israeli forces, said Alakbarov.
The pattern is clear. Palestinian populations are increasingly being forcibly displaced from villages across the West Bank before settlers seize the vacated land.
Settler attacks were previously concentrated in Area C, which is under full Israeli control.
They are increasingly being reported in Area B, which is under Palestinian civil control and joint Israeli-Palestinian security control, and even in Area A, which is under full Palestinian control, he said.
Alongside the mounting violence, Israel is significantly accelerating its settlement activities while consolidating its control across the occupied West Bank.
Since the beginning of the year, Israeli planning authorities advanced or approved approximately 12,360 housing units in the occupied West Bank – 7,200 housing units in Area C and 5,160 housing units in East Jerusalem, he said.

Title: Subsidised cooking oil diverted for used-oil resale, 3,150kg seized
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM: The Penang Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) seized 3,150kg of subsidised packet cooking oil during an integrated Ops Tiris 4.0 raid.
Penang KPDN director S. Jegan said the seizure followed a month-long intelligence operation targeting three premises, with a 51-year-old local man detained to assist investigations.
He said enforcement officers raided the premises yesterday with about 2,300kg of one-kilogramme packet cooking oil seized at the first two locations and another 850kg found as excess stock at a licensed premises.
"The interesting part of this case is that the excess cooking oil was not intended to be supplied to the public. It was being processed into used oil for resale," he told newsmen here today.
Jegan said investigators found empty cooking oil packets that had been cut open, two knives believed to have been used to cut the packets and a pump and hose set.
They also found an empty 1,000-litre Intermediate Bulk Container (IBC) tank, an electrical weighing scale, a copy of a Retail Controlled Supply Act (CSA) licence, company registration documents and three baskets.
A Nissan Navara four-wheel-drive vehicle was also seized, with the total value of the seized items estimated at RM95,000.
Jegan said the licensed premises had been authorised to store up to 1,000kg of subsidised cooking oil but was found to have 1,850kg, resulting in an excess of about 850kg.
"Based on our initial inspection and investigation, two offences are suspected under the Control of Supplies Act 1961 and related regulations, namely Section 20(1) of the Act and Regulation 10(1) of the Control of Supplies Regulations 1974," he added.
He said the suspect would be remanded at the Kulim magistrate's court to facilitate further investigations.
Jegan said the suspect allegedly bought subsidised cooking oil packets, cut them open, mixed the oil with colouring and transferred it into the IBC tank before selling it as used oil for RM3.50.
"The profit is RM1 per packet, without having to worry about finding retailers. There are many places that collect used cooking oil, so there is a ready market," he said.
Jegan said the practice was worrying as subsidised cooking oil meant to benefit consumers was being diverted and processed for other purposes.
"Subsidies are provided by the government to help the people who need them. We are concerned that they are being misused in this way," he said.
He said individuals found guilty under the Control of Supplies Act could face a fine of up to RM1 million for a first offence and up to RM3 million for subsequent offences, or imprisonment of up to three years, or both.
Companies convicted of similar offences can face fines of up to RM2 million for a first offence and up to RM5 million for subsequent offences.
"KPDN takes the misappropriation of subsidised controlled goods seriously as such activities can affect supply and deprive consumers of the benefits of government subsidies," he said.
Jegan said Penang KPDN would intensify enforcement operations to curb leakage involving subsidised controlled goods and take firm action against those found violating the law.

Title: Man with criminal record charged with robbing, injuring Indian citizen
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A man with previous criminal and drug offences pleaded not guilty to robbing and injuring an Indian citizen at Taman Nusantara here recently.
Mohd Salim Kapoor Rahim, 40, made the plea after the charge was read before Sessions Court Judge Irwan Suainbon.
He was charged with robbing the victim and intentionally causing him hurt in front of a house at Block A-2-5, Taman Nusantara, Jalan Makloom, about 4.20pm on Aug 8.
The charge under Section 394 of the Penal Code carries a prison term of up to 20 years and a fine or whipping upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Anuarul Hakim Abdul Muen offered RM10,000 bail with additional conditions that the accused report to the police station, refrain from contacting the victim and prosecution witnesses, and surrender his passport to the court.
However, the accused, who was unrepresented, appealed for a lower bail amount, saying he was unemployed and his wife would provide the bail.
The court allowed bail at RM7,000 with the additional conditions sought by the prosecution.
The case will be mentioned on Sept 15 for document submission and the appointment of a lawyer.
It is learnt that the accused had gone to the homestay where the victim was staying and identified himself as a police officer before asking the victim to produce his passport.
He allegedly then struck the victim with a padlock before snatching his mobile phone and fleeing.
The victim reportedly suffered injuries to his nose and back in the incident.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cross-border e-commerce opens global markets for Malaysian MSMEs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Cross-border e-commerce is emerging as a key gateway for Malaysian micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to tap global markets, with the eTRADE 2.0 programme generating RM438.7 million in actual export sales.
The programme, spearheaded by the Malaysia External Trade Development Corp (Matrade), has supported more than 2,000 MSMEs through grants, training, technical guidance and capacity-building initiatives.
Participating companies have expanded into 163 export markets, including less conventional destinations such as Réunion Island, Kiribati and Nauru, according to findings from the eTRADE 2.0 programme.
"Asean remained the main export destination, with about 30 per cent of participating companies strengthening their presence in the region," it said.
The study also found that ready-to-eat food, beverages, pharmaceutical and cosmetic products, household goods and plastic products were among the best-performing categories.
It noted that at least 852 new products were listed on international e-commerce platforms, further expanding the presence of Malaysian products in global markets.
The programme also contributed to employment creation, with at least 661 jobs generated among participating companies.
In terms of inclusivity, the study showed 48 per cent of beneficiaries were Bumiputera-owned companies, while women-owned and youth-owned companies accounted for 33 per cent and 9 per cent, respectively.
Alibaba.com was the cross-border e-commerce platform that recorded the highest export sales value among the programme's beneficiaries.
Matrade chief executive officer Datuk Indera Abu Bakar Yusof said the eTRADE 2.0 programme has successfully demonstrated that a digital-led approach can strengthen the competitiveness of MSMEs, encourage job creation and support a stronger domestic supply chain.
Indera said these achievements will continue to serve as a guide for MATRADE's ongoing efforts to empower MSMEs in the global digital economy.
"The impact study not only provided an overview of the effectiveness of the eTRADE 2.0 programme but also provided strategic input for Matrade in formulating more targeted, inclusive and sustainable digital export development interventions," he said.
Following the success of eTRADE 2.0, Matrade will continue strengthening the cross-border e-commerce ecosystem through the eBizLink 2.0 programme.
The programme will focus on expanding access to international markets, enhancing MSME capabilities, developing the digital trade ecosystem and strengthening strategic partnerships with global e-commerce platforms.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Dr Wan Azizah: Anwar expected to be discharged from hospital today
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is expected to be discharged from hospital today after receiving treatment, his wife Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail said.
She said Anwar expressed his appreciation to everyone who had prayed for his health and well-being.
"PMX sends his regards and thanked everyone who has prayed for his health and recovery," she said.
She spoke to reporters after attending the Semarak Merdeka programme in conjunction with the 2026 National Month celebrations at the Bandar Tun Razak branch of the Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) here.
Anwar had successfully undergone an elective laparoscopic surgical procedure to treat a para-umbilical hernia on Monday. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Durian orchard caretaker fined RM7,500 over fake gun, criminal intimidation
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A durian orchard caretaker was fined RM7,500 by the magistrate's court today after pleading guilty to possessing a fake firearm and criminal intimidation.
Choong Ah Cheng, 57, entered the plea after both charges were read to him before magistrate Nadratun Naim Mohd Saidi.
On the first charge, Choong admitted to unlawfully possessing a fake firearm, a Hatsan AT44-10 QE air rifle bearing serial number 041521754, in his hut at a durian orchard in Bukit Gambir here at 10pm on Aug 5.
He was charged under Section 36(1) of the Arms Act 1960, punishable under Section 36 of the same Act by up to one year's imprisonment or a fine of up to RM5,000, or both, upon conviction.
On the second charge, Choong admitted to criminally intimidating a 42-year-old man by threatening to cause him serious injury at the same durian orchard about 5pm on Aug 4.
He was charged under Section 506 of the Penal Code, which provides for up to seven years' imprisonment, a fine, or both, upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Ahmad Danial Amir Saad urged the court to impose an appropriate sentence.
However, counsel Shariffah Farveen Syed Ibrahim, representing Choong, appealed for a minimum fine, saying her client had a wife and daughter to support and worked as an orchard caretaker without a fixed income.
"My client regrets his actions and has pledged not to repeat the offences," she told the court.
After hearing submissions from both sides, Nadratun fined Choong RM3,000 for the fake firearm possession charge, in default of eight months' jail.
For the criminal intimidation charge, he was fined RM4,500, in default of nine months' jail.
The court was told that the threat stemmed from a misunderstanding between Choong and the victim over access to the durian orchard.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rwanda to name 22 baby gorillas as conservation, tourism continue to grow
Article:
KIGALI: Rwanda will name 22 baby mountain gorillas born over the past 12 months on Sept 4 during the 21st edition of the Kwita Izina gorilla-naming ceremony, officials announced on Tuesday, reported Xinhua.
The ceremony will be held at the foothills of Volcanoes National Park in Musanze District, northern Rwanda, according to Eugene Mutangana, executive secretary of the Rwanda Nature Foundation.
Kwita Izina has become a major conservation and tourism event, highlighting Rwanda's efforts to protect mountain gorillas while linking wildlife conservation to tourism, community development and sustainable economic growth.
Speaking at a press conference in Kigali, the Rwandan capital, Mutangana said the annual ceremony reflects Rwanda's belief that conservation should benefit both nature and people.
"For over two decades, Kwita Izina has showcased Rwanda's belief that conservation is not simply about protecting wildlife.
"It is about creating opportunities for people, supporting communities, growing tourism and ensuring that future generations inherit a healthy and thriving natural environment," he said.
"At this year's Kwita Izina, 22 baby mountain gorillas will receive names, marking another important chapter in this conservation journey," Mutangana said.
Since the first official Kwita Izina in 2005, 438 mountain gorillas have been named, according to Mutangana.
Rwanda's tourism industry generated a record US$685 million (RM2.8 billion) in revenues in 2025, up from US$647 million in 2024, while visitor arrivals reached 1.49 million, representing a nine-percent year-on-year increase, according to the Rwanda Development Board. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PPA Asia Tour brings world-class pickleball action to KL next month
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: World-class pickleball is set to take centre stage in Kuala Lumpur this September as the Leapmotor Kuala Lumpur Cup 2026 brings five days of Professional Pickleball Association (PPA) Asia Tour action to The Hood.
Running from Sept 9 to 13, the tournament will see some of the world's biggest pickleball stars descend on Kuala Lumpur, giving fans the chance to watch top-level competition up close.
Media Prima is the official media partner for the tournament, which promises more than action on the court.
Pickletown will be set up throughout the event, offering food, games, giveaways, exclusive merchandise and activities to complement the tournament atmosphere.
FLEXIBLE ENTRY
Fans can choose from a range of passes, with every ticket providing access to the Championship Court, Grandstand Court and Pickletown.
Those who do not want to miss a moment can opt for the Dinker GA Season Pass, which provides access across all five days, including general seating and Pickletown, with re-entry permitted throughout the tournament.

Banger ticket holders will be seated in the GA Left Stand, directly behind the players, while Dinker ticket holders will have access to the GA Right Stand.
For a more premium experience, the VIP Pass offers reserved seating and prime-time pickleball viewing, as well as access to the VIP Lounge with complimentary food and beverages.
VIP guests will also have opportunities to meet professional players during special meet-and-greet sessions.
Those looking to get even closer to the action can opt for the Premium Courtside Pass, which offers front-row seating at the Championship Court.
The package includes VIP Lounge access, complimentary food and beverages, professional player meet-and-greet sessions, priority gate access and an official tournament merchandise pack worth more than RM2,000.
OFFICIAL MERCHANDISE ON OFFER
Meanwhile, official Leapmotor Kuala Lumpur Cup merchandise will be available at the venue throughout the five-day event, with tour shirts, mini paddles, collectible toys and more on offer.
The merchandise is exclusive to the event and will be available while stocks last.
Fans can also pre-order a limited number of merchandise vouchers through the
event website
before the tournament to receive additional value on their purchases at the event store.
For those unable to make it to the venue, the PPA Tour will also be available to watch live on
Tonton
.

Title: Wrong to draw conclusions on TH given RCI's limited scope, says BN's Zambry
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: It is inappropriate for any party to draw sweeping conclusions about the Lembaga Tabung Haji issue, as the scope of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into the pilgrimage fund was "limited", says Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir.
The Barisan Nasional secretary-general said the RCI's scope was limited to 2014 to 2020, and that developments and decisions made after 2020 should be considered.
Commenting on the special parliamentary sitting on the report, Zambry said the report's tabling and subsequent debate by MPs demonstrated transparency in the matter.
"BN's position is clear and consistent: there is nothing to hide from the rakyat, especially the 10 million Tabung Haji depositors," he said when contacted.
He said the RCI was a mechanism established under the country's laws to investigate matters of public interest, and its findings should be examined objectively based on facts and evidence rather than used as an instrument of political condemnation.
"Yesterday's debate also confirmed that this RCI focuses only on the period from 2014 to 2020.
"It would therefore be inappropriate to draw sweeping conclusions about the entire history of TH's governance without also examining other periods, including developments and decisions made after 2020," he said.
Zambry said BN had, from the outset, supported the tabling and debate of the RCI report in Parliament.
He said BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi had also proposed that the scope of scrutiny be expanded, if necessary, to ensure comprehensive transparency.
"This clearly shows that BN has never taken the position of closing the space for public scrutiny on the TH issue," he said.
Zambry said the focus should now be on institutional reforms, particularly issues raised by the RCI concerning governance, concentration of power, separation of functions and checks and balances.
"These matters should be viewed as a foundation for strengthening the TH institution, rather than merely as an opportunity for short-term political gain," he said.
Zambry also urged all parties to prioritise the interests of TH depositors and avoid what he described as reckless accusations, political judgments before legal processes were completed and narratives that could undermine depositor confidence without a responsible factual basis.
"TH is not merely a financial entity. It is an institution of the Muslim community entrusted with the management of savings, investments, and the sacred responsibility of facilitating the pilgrimage," he said.
BN welcomes the improvement measures that have already been implemented, including the adoption of a substantial portion of the RCI recommendations, and believes that institutional reforms must continue consistently.
"The focus should no longer be on creating the perception that any party is attempting to conceal the truth, but ensuring that TH's governance continues to be strengthened, all reform recommendations are implemented, and that depositors remain confident in TH," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rod Stewart cancels remainder of US tour after heart operation
Article:
LONDON: British singer Rod Stewart has cancelled the remainder of his 2026 United States (US) tour dates after undergoing heart surgery, reported PA Media/dpa.
The 81-year-old singer confirmed on Instagram that he will take four weeks off to recover after undergoing a coronary stent procedure, effectively cutting short his US and Mexico performances, which were due to continue into September.
"I'm already feeling better and very much on the mend," he said.
"I want to thank the doctors, nurses and everyone who has taken such wonderful care of me.
"I am deeply disappointed to miss these shows and sorry to let my fans down, but I look forward to getting back on stage and having a good time with you all again soon."
He was scheduled to perform events across Ohio, Illinois and Mexico, as well as a six-night stretch at Caesars Palace in Las Vegas.
His representatives said Stewart was "doing very well" following the procedure and had "returned to his normal daily activities".
The statement added: "On the advice of his doctors, he will take the next four weeks to recuperate and regain full fitness before returning to the stage.
"Unfortunately, this means he will be unable to continue his current tour dates.
"Information regarding affected performances will be communicated by the respective promoters and venues."
Two further dates in Colorado are scheduled for September 2027.
The announcement came after Stewart postponed shows in Cincinnati and Cleveland following medical concerns.
Cleveland's Rocket Arena earlier confirmed the cancellation on social media, writing: "Following a period of monitoring, doctors have advised Rod Stewart to rest for at least 48 hours. As a result, his performance tomorrow night, August 11, 2026 at Rocket Arena in Cleveland has been cancelled.
"Rod is disappointed to miss the show and appreciates everyone's understanding. He looks forward to returning to the stage soon."
Health problems had also forced the cancellation and postponement of shows in May and June.
In May, the
Maggie May
singer sent "apologies to my family of fans" in a statement to the Las Vegas Review-Journal after cancelling performances in Nevada, adding: "I am on vocal rest as I recover from a sinus infection."
Less than a month later, he cancelled his San Diego show after being diagnosed with a respiratory infection that resulted in laryngitis.
Earlier this month, the rocker welcomed his sixth grandchild after his daughter Ruby gave birth to a son called Levi. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: SWCorp investigates alleged dumping of Singapore construction waste in Pontian
Article:
JOHOR BARU: The Solid Waste Management and Public Cleansing Corporation (SWCorp) is investigating the origin of construction and demolition waste allegedly brought from Singapore and dumped at several locations in Pontian.
Johor Health and Environment Committee chairman Ling Tian Soon said SWCorp was looking at where the waste came from.
"SWCorp is carrying out investigations to establish the source of the waste, including whether it originated from Singapore," he told the
New Straits Times
.
SWCorp said  in a statement to
NST
that an investigation paper into the alleged dumping of construction waste from Singapore at a site in Mukim Sungai Karang, Pontian, had been opened.
Initial checks found that the site was not a gazetted facility for solid waste management, and no permit or approval had been issued for the import or management of construction waste.
"SWCorp has never issued any permit or granted permission for construction waste to be brought into or managed at the location, including for land reclamation," the statement said.
Investigation is being conducted under Section 14 of the Solid Waste and Public Cleansing Management Act 2007 (Act 672).
SWCorp mounted surveillance and monitoring at the site on Aug 8 to track lorry movements and detect any waste disposal or management activities.
So far, it has found no lorry movement or waste disposal activity.
The reclamation work has also stopped and the site has been barricaded, the statement said.
The company said it would continue its surveillance to detect any renewed activity and enable further enforcement action, while action has been taken against the landowner for using the site for waste management activities without a licence.
State Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor had said the alleged dumping could not be allowed to continue if the waste was indeed brought into Johor without the necessary permits or approvals.
The issue has also raised questions on how such consignments, if they originated from Singapore, were transported across the border and whether the relevant import, transport and disposal requirements had been met.
NST
has reached out to Singaporean authorities, including the Singapore High Commission in Kuala Lumpur, but has not received a response as of press time.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Form Two boy found drowned in Kuala Krai river, search continues for friend
Article:
KUALA KRAI: One of two Form Two boys missing while swimming in a river near Kampung Aur Duri yesterday was found drowned this morning.
The body of Lut Na'iman Mohd Noor Aziron, 14, was discovered at 9.10am by the Fire and Rescue Department Water Rescue Unit, about 40 minutes after the search and rescue operation resumed.
Kuala Krai Fire and Rescue station chief Senior Fire Officer Nik Ahmad Afsham Nik Pa said the victim was found at a depth of three metres and 50 metres from where he was last seen.
He said the body was handed over to the police and taken to the Forensic Unit of Sultan Ismail Petra Hospital.
"However, another victim, Muhamad Rayyan Hakimie Mohd Yusmiza, 14, has yet to be found and search efforts are ongoing. The search radius has been expanded to 500 metres from where the victim was last seen.
"This surface search radius was expanded to locate the victim as quickly as possible," he told reporters at the scene.
He added that the operation involved 12 personnel from the Kuala Krai station and six water rescue unit members from the Pengkalan Chepa and Pengkalan Kubor stations.
Yesterday, it
was reported that
an outing involving five friends swimming in the river turned into a tragedy when two of them went missing, feared drowned.
The search operation was launched yesterday but had to be suspended until today due to poor weather conditions.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Preschool teacher charged with sexual assault of 8-year-old pupil
Article:
SEREMBAN: A preschool teacher was charged in the Sessions Court today with two counts of committing physical sexual assault against an 8-year-old male pupil in April.
Muhamad Shazali Sharipudin, 42, pleaded not guilty after the charges were read to him before judge Tasnim Abu Bakar.
According to the two separate charges, the accused allegedly committed the acts inside a preschool classroom at a school in Rembau at 10am on April 1 and 9am on April 3.
He was charged under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, which carries a maximum prison term of 20 years and whipping upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Nurul Balkis Zunaidi offered bail at RM20,000 with two additional conditions.
Defence lawyer Syed Amirul Syed Edros requested a reasonable bail amount, stating that his client is a civil servant who has served as a preschool teacher for 17 years, earns a net monthly income of RM4,000, is single, and supports his mother.
He added that his client has been transferred to the Rembau district education office, no longer teaches at the school, and poses no flight risk.
The court allowed bail at RM8,000 for both charges, with additional conditions that the accused must not harass the victim or witnesses, report to a police station monthly, and surrender his passport.
Case mention was fixed for Sept 15 for document submission.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Aiman Athirah: Claims over Dengkil PPR's delay, safety, cost inaccurate
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Housing and Local Government Ministry today dismissed allegations surrounding the Ampar Tenang People's Housing Project (PPR) in Dengkil, describing claims concerning safety, delays and infrastructure as inaccurate.
Deputy Minister Datuk Aiman Athirah Sabu said the damage reported on Jan 15 was caused by an unusually severe storm that affected the roof structures of 46 units.
Aiman Athirah, who also chairs the Task Force on Sick and Abandoned Private Housing Projects, said an emergency allocation of RM263,000 was approved for repairs.
"The repair works were technically evaluated and certified 100 per cent safe for occupation before the Phase 2 key handover on April 2," she said in a statement today.
Addressing claims that the project had been delayed by up to 10 years, Aiman Athirah said PPR Ampar Tenang obtained its Certificate of Completion and Compliance (CCC) on Dec 31 under the current government.
"The ministry continued repair works even after the Defect Liability Period ended on June 13," she added.
As of April 2, a total of 212 of the 393 residents had received their keys.
On ownership costs, she clarified that the actual construction cost exceeded RM215,000 per unit, but buyers only needed to pay RM20,000 to Perbadanan Nasional Bhd, with no additional charges.
"The government absorbed a full subsidy of RM88 million.
"PPR Ampar Tenang was built with high-quality facilities to benefit the local community," she said.
Each 750 sq ft unit features three bedrooms and two bathrooms.
"The entire project secured a 100 per cent CCC, proving it met all required standards before occupancy," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Housewife charged with murder of 16-month-old step-granddaughter
Article:
KOTA TINGGI: A 39-year-old housewife was charged in the Magistrate's Court here today for murdering her 16-month-old step-granddaughter last month.
No plea was recorded from the accused, Nurul Farhana Laili Shah, who appeared before magistrate Hafizah Abdul Rajak.
Nurul Farhana was charged with murdering Nur Anggun Dahlia Abdullah at Jalan SS6/13, Taman Sri Saujana, here, between 12.30pm on July 30 and 9.30am the following day.
The charge under Section 302 of the Penal Code carries the death penalty or imprisonment of up to 40 years and, if the death penalty is not imposed, whipping of not less than 12 strokes.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Nor Afiqah Musa appeared for the prosecution, while the accused was represented by lawyer Lydiana Mansor.
The court fixed Dec 12 for mention pending the completion of the chemical, post-mortem and deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) reports.
No bail was granted.
Yesterday, Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said the woman, who was the baby's step-grandmother, was arrested after the child was allegedly
abused to death
.
He said the woman had cared for the baby since birth after the child's 18-year-old unmarried mother, who was still studying at a vocational college in the state, left her in the woman's care.
Police initially investigated the case under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001 after the woman lodged a report claiming that the baby had died she was asleep.
However, a post-mortem found that the child had died from blunt-force trauma to the abdomen and chest.
The examination also found wounds and bruises on the child's body, believed to have been caused by abuse.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Teleport strengthens Australia network through Avalon Airport
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Capital A Bhd's logistics arm, Teleport, has partnered with Avalon Airport Melbourne to establish a new strategic operations hub in Victoria, Australia.
Through the agreement, Avalon Airport will serve as Teleport's latest Australian hub, supporting the movement of cargo and e-commerce shipments across key Asian trade routes and Australia through the airport's dedicated freight infrastructure.
Teleport currently handles its Australian cargo flows through major gateway hubs including Melbourne, Sydney, Brisbane and Perth from key markets such as mainland China, Hong Kong, India, Malaysia and Vietnam.
According to Teleport's CEO Pete Chareonwongsak, Avalon Airport is the right fit for Teleport's growth plans, as it delivers curfew-free capacity processing, fast turnarounds and the flexibility to handle eCommerce alongside general cargo.
"Our proven history of scaling throughput across primary hubs like Kuala Lumpur, and secondary hubs like Don Mueang, and Phuket in Thailand and Bali in Indonesia, gives us full confidence in the massive potential this partnership will deliver for the region.
"We believe secondary hubs are a proven engine for air cargo growth," said Pete in a statement.
The Avalon hub marks the next phase of the company's international expansion strategy across Oceania, the Middle East and Europe in collaboration with its airline partners.
Teleport said the partnership comes amid growing demand for cross-border e-commerce with Australians spending nearly A$19 billion on online platforms in 2025, representing a 13 per cent year-on-year increase.
Teleport's growing customer base includes major Chinese e-commerce marketplaces, and the new hub is expected to provide faster and more reliable access to Australian consumers.
Avalon Airport Melbourne chief executive officer Ari Suss said the collaboration represents an important milestone in the airport's efforts to become a leading freight and logistics gateway.
The partnership is expected to strengthen Victoria's international trade links, diversify Australia's freight capacity and support further growth in the state's logistics sector.
Teleport plans to begin the first phase of operations in the second half of 2026, initially focusing on moving e-commerce shipments from China into Avalon Airport.
Founded in 2018, Teleport has expanded its asset-light logistics network to become the largest air logistics provider in Southeast Asia and the ninth-largest in Asia by cargo volume, according to WorldACD.
Its Teleport Network currently connects more than 290 cities across 80 countries through partnerships with over 55 airlines.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Taiwan condemns China's plan for navy drill with Indonesia off island's east
Article:
TAIPEI, Aug 12 — Taiwan has condemned China’s plan to hold a navy drill with Indonesia this month off the democratic island’s east coast, saying Beijing seeks to create the “false impression” that it has jurisdiction over the area.
China claims Taiwan is part of its territory and insists it has authority over the waters surrounding the island, which Taipei rejects.
The Chinese defence ministry said yesterday one of its warships and an Indonesian frigate will conduct a “passage exercise” east of Taiwan in mid-August to “enhance the joint operational capabilities of the two navies” and “jointly safeguard regional peace and stability”.
Taiwan’s top China policy body hit back late yesterday, saying it “strongly condemned the CCP military provocation”, referring to the Chinese Communist Party.
“This move is, in reality... aimed at creating the false impression for the international community that the CCP has jurisdiction over waters east of Taiwan and blatantly infringing upon our national sovereignty and maritime rights and interests,” the Mainland Affairs Council (MAC) said in a statement.
The Indonesian military did not immediately respond to AFP’s request for comment.
China’s announcement came as Taiwan holds its largest military drills of the year, aimed at preparing its population for a potential Chinese invasion.
Beijing deploys warships, fighter jets and coast guard vessels around Taiwan on an almost daily basis to assert its claim of sovereignty.
In June, Chinese ships began to patrol an area of the Western Pacific near Taiwan’s east coast, which Taipei branded as “provocative” and “expansionism in disguise”.
During that operation, the China Coast Guard for the first time radioed cargo ships passing Taiwan for information about their crew and destination.
That was followed last week by China’s Guangdong Maritime Safety Administration announcing “traffic control measures” for the Taiwan Strait as Typhoon Dolphin swept towards the region.
Ships entering the sensitive waterway from the south would be “required to strictly comply with the traffic control regulations, seek shelter in safe waters, and follow the instructions of on-site maritime authorities to ensure safety,” the August 5 announcement said.
Taiwan’s MAC described the order as a “trampling of the international order and norms” and “utterly ridiculous”. — AFP

Title: Six schools in Sarawak shift to online learning as haze hits ‘very unhealthy’ levels
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 12 — Six schools in the Tebedu district have been ordered to temporarily close after the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading there exceeded 200 amid worsening haze conditions.
The Sarawak Education Department (JPNS) said the precautionary measure was taken in line with the Education Ministry’s (MOE) guidelines, with the safety, health and wellbeing of students and school staff given priority.
As of 10.30am today, the schools involved are SK Sejijag, with 51 students and 14 staff; SK Sungai Sameran (129 students, 21 staff); SK Tepoi (42 students, 15 staff); SK Entubuh (67 students, 18 staff); SK Temong (205 students, 21 staff); and SK Tema (85 students, 15 staff).
According to JPNS, these schools are under the administration of the Serian District Education Office (Serian PPD).
JPNS also reminded principals and headmasters that they do not need to wait for specific instructions from the PPD or JPNS to close schools when the API reading in their respective areas or districts exceeds 200.
“Under MOE Circular No. 1 of 2019 on measures to safeguard the health and safety of students in schools located in areas considered critical due to haze, all schools in areas or districts where the API exceeds 200 must be closed immediately.
“Principals and headmasters must act promptly based on the current API readings in their respective areas and do not need to wait for closure instructions from the PPD or JPNS.
“At the same time, schools must inform the PPD and JPNS of the closure immediately for coordination, monitoring and record-keeping,” the department said.
JPNS said home-based teaching and learning (PdPR) would continue online during the temporary closure to ensure students’ learning was not disrupted.
The department added that schools have also been instructed to maintain communication with parents and guardians while giving due attention to the health and welfare of students throughout the closure.
Regarding the situation in Serian, whereby haze has also worsened, JPNS said the department through PPD Serian will continue monitoring API readings and air quality by obtaining updates from the authorities and relevant agencies.
Schools have also been reminded to closely monitor API readings in their respective areas and take appropriate action in accordance with MOE guidelines.
The department said the decision on the reopening of schools will take into account the latest API readings, prevailing conditions and directives or guidelines in force.
JPNS stressed that the safety and wellbeing of students and all education personnel remained its priority, adding that prompt and appropriate action based on established guidelines was necessary to minimise exposure to health risks caused by haze.
“Parents and guardians are urged to ensure their children remain safe and follow official updates issued by the schools, PPD Serian and JPNS.
“They are also advised not to rely on unofficial information or wait for additional instructions once a school had announced its closure based on an API reading exceeding 200,” added JPNS. — The Borneo Post

Title: Wong Chen joins Bersama after resigning as Subang MP
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — Former Subang MP Wong Chen has joined Bersama, days after resigning from his parliamentary seat.
Bersama chairman Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli announced Wong’s membership at a press conference at the party’s headquarters in Taman Putra Perdana, Puchong, today.
Wong, a three-term MP who had been with PKR for nearly two decades, had previously indicated that he would eventually leave the party after Rafizi and Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad resigned their parliamentary seats to lead Bersama.
Wong was among three PKR MPs whose access to the MyKhas constituency funding portal was revoked after they attended Bersama’s launch event in May. The other two were Ampang MP Rodziah Ismail and Petaling Jaya MP Lee Chean Chung.
Wong was previously the non-executive chairman of Malaysia Debt Ventures Bhd but was removed from the position in May.
MORE TO COME

Title: MEF urges govt to act faster before MSME cash crunch turns into job losses
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — The Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) is calling on the government to strengthen assistance for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
It noted that businesses continue to face pressures from rising operating and labour costs, financing constraints, weaker cash flows, supply-chain disruptions, regulatory requirements and intense market competition.
MEF president Datuk Dr Syed Hussain Syed Husman has proposed that the government consider introducing a coordinated MSME survival and resilience package to help businesses navigate ongoing cost and cash-flow pressures.
He said the package should include targeted and temporary tax relief, faster and simpler access to financing and greater use of cash-flow-based lending.
“Under this package, the government should consider expanding government-backed guarantees, temporary regulatory and compliance relief, faster payments to MSME suppliers, greater MSME access to government procurement and employment retention support,” he said in a statement today.
He stressed that MSME policy must ultimately be viewed through the lens of employment and economic sustainability.
“Helping viable MSMEs survive is itself an important way of protecting workers because these businesses provide employment to millions of Malaysians and support extensive domestic supply chains.
“Our objective is not to keep inefficient businesses alive indefinitely or prevent viable businesses from being pushed into closure because of temporary cash-flow and cost pressures beyond their control,” he said.
MEF said it is ready to work closely with the Ministry of Entrepreneur and Cooperative Development (KUSKOP), the Ministry of Finance (MoF), Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) and other relevant agencies to ensure that MSME assistance is practical, accessible and responsive to actual business conditions.
“MSMEs have shown remarkable resilience through repeated economic challenges. They have continued to employ Malaysians, support local suppliers and contribute to the economy even when their own margins are under pressure.
“They now need a stronger and more comprehensive safety net. The government has already taken important steps. MEF’s call is for us to go further – faster, more targeted and with greater urgency – before temporary business difficulties become permanent closures and job losses,” added Syed Hussain. — Bernama

Title: Waiting for your university offer? UPUOnline results out Aug 14 noon
Article:

Results can be checked from 12 noon, August 14 to 5 pm, August 23 online via the links https://upu.mohe.gov.my,

Article:

The body of Luth Naiman Mohd Noraziron was found by members of the Water Rescue Team (PPDA) of the Kelantan Fire and Rescue Department at 9.10 am, about 100 metres from the incident site.
