Title: Selangor Rail Line still in planning stage, completion targeted for 2060
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 12 — The Selangor government is still in the discussion stage with various parties including the private sector to identify the appropriate development and financing model for the development of the Selangor Rail Line.
State Investment, Trade and Mobility Exco Ng Sze Han said the state government through the Menteri Besar of Selangor (Incorporated) or MBI as the Technical Committee for Selangor Rail Development is examining the most potential development and financing model to be implemented.
He said the mechanism for implementing the development of the Selangor Rail Line is also being refined to identify the most profitable and appropriate method.
“Of course, a large-scale project like the Selangor Rail Line involves the private sector as well as government agencies,” he said in response to a question from Mariam Abdul Rashid (PH-Meru) regarding the direction of the Selangor Rail Line project at the Selangor State Legislative Assembly sitting today.
Meanwhile, he said based on the feasibility study that has been carried out, the first phase of the project’s development is expected to take 10 years, covering the entire development process including the preparation of preliminary designs, detailed studies and approval of the Railway Scheme by the Land Public Transport Agency (APAD).
“The phase also includes procurement, land acquisition, construction work and the testing and commissioning process.”
“The final phase of development is expected to be completed in 2060, subject to the implementation of the planned development phases,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Kedah fails to overturn ruling against refusal to renew pool betting, lottery licences
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 — The Kedah government has failed to overturn a ruling that barred it from refusing to renew licences for pool betting and lottery operators.
Free Malaysia Today
(FMT) reported that a Federal Court panel chaired by Justice Datuk Rhodzariah Bujang held that the legal questions proposed by the state government failed to meet the threshold for determination by the court.
Justices Datuk Collin Lawrence Sequerah and Datuk Azmi Ariffin sat with Rhodzariah.
The questions centred on whether the courts could inquire into the legality of the state government’s decision and the state’s powers under the Federal Constitution.
The court also ordered the Kedah government to pay RM50,000 in costs.
Last year, the Court of Appeal, in a majority decision, ruled that the state government’s move to deny licence renewals for several pool betting agents, their companies and officers was unconstitutional.
It said matters concerning pool betting and lotteries fell within the purview of the Finance Ministry. The court also held that the Kedah government’s refusal to renew the operators’ premise licences had the effect of usurping the Finance Minister’s powers and imposing a blanket ban on pool betting and lotteries.
According to FMT, the court further reminded the state government that its powers were confined to matters under the Ninth Schedule of the Federal Constitution and the Local Government Act 1976.
“However, the refusal (to issue and renew business licences) reflected a policy objection to betting and lotteries, rather than concerns about the building or premises they occupied,” Justice Faizah Jamaluddin was quoted as saying in the majority ruling.
She also noted that licences issued by the Finance Minister were subject to strict federal conditions, including requirements such as printing a note on tickets that gambling is prohibited for Muslims.
Chief Judge of Sabah and Sarawak Azizah Nawawi dissented, holding that the Kedah executive council’s decision fell within its legal scope under the Local Government Act and that the courts should not interfere.
The report said lawyer Azhar Harun appeared for the state government, while Brian Foong, Hiqmar Danial Hidzir and Eolanda Yeo represented the pool betting agents, companies and officers.

Title: High Court orders Rosmah to pay RM67.4m into stakeholder account pending appeal in missing jewellery suit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor was today ordered by the High Court to pay RM67.4 million into a joint stakeholder account within a month, pending her appeal in a suit filed by Lebanese jeweller Global Royalty Trading SAL to recover the value of 43 jewellery items delivered to her.
Rosmah had previously sought to stay the execution of the High Court’s June 10 decision, with the court having fixed today to deliver its
decision
on the application.
In granting the order, Judicial Commissioner Marianne Antoinette Ghani said a stay was not automatically granted simply because an appeal was pending, further stating that Rosmah — as the defendant — had to prove special circumstances justified her application for a stay.
She said Rosmah’s contention that the judgment sum was too large for an individual to pay could not, by itself, justify a stay of execution, despite her claim that her jewellery had been seized during a raid by a third party.
“In the circumstances, the Court orders that a conditional stay of execution be granted to the defendant pending her appeal to the Court of Appeal.
“The defendant shall pay the judgment sum into a joint stakeholders account between the solicitors for the parties within one month from this order, failing which the plaintiff will be at liberty to take out execution proceedings as it deems fit in the circumstances pending the determination of the defendant’s appeal to the Court of Appeal,” she said.
In her judgment, Marianne said the court found that a conditional stay requiring the defendant to pay the judgment sum into a joint stakeholder account would best balance both parties’ rights.
“This will ensure that the plaintiff as the successful litigant is assured the fruit of its successful litigation and avoid the prejudice caused by an unconditional stay if the appeal is dismissed.
“Whilst ensuring that the defendant’s rights of appeal shall not be rendered nugatory should her appeal be allowed, as the judgement funds shall remain within the jurisdiction and are easily, therefore, recoverable, preventing her appeal from being rendered nugatory,” she said.
She also said the court was bound by a previous ruling which established that a substantial judgment sum, on its own, did not constitute a special circumstance.
Rosmah had previously argued that Global Royalty was a foreign entity with no business presence or assets in Malaysia, creating a real risk that the judgment sum could be transferred out of the jurisdiction or dissipated if she succeeded on appeal.
Lawyer Reza Rahim appeared for Rosmah while Datuk David Gurupatham appeared for Global Royalty.
The present case centred on 44 pieces of luxury jewellery worth RM67,461,027.37 (US$14.57 million) that Global Royalty said were delivered to Rosmah in 2018 for viewing under a consignment arrangement.
Global Royalty later filed a legal suit in 2023, seeking the return of the items or payment for their value after claiming the items were supplied to Rosmah on consignment but were never returned following their seizure during a 2018 police raid at Pavilion Residences.
Only one item — a diamond and emerald bracelet — was eventually recovered and returned to the Lebanese company following separate forfeiture proceedings.

Title: Putrajaya chokes as unhealthy air readings climb across Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — Eight areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as at 9 am today, comprising six in Sarawak and two in Peninsular Malaysia.
According to the Department of Environment’s (DOE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, Sarikei in Sarawak recorded the highest reading at 161.
Other areas in Sarawak with unhealthy readings were Bintulu and Sri Aman, both at 157, followed by Samalaju (153), Sibu (151) and Miri (130).
In Peninsular Malaysia, Putrajaya recorded an API reading of 114, while another area also recorded an unhealthy reading of above 100.
Meanwhile, 51 areas recorded moderate API readings (51 to 100), and four areas recorded good air quality readings (below 50).
An API reading between zero and 50 indicates good air quality; 51 to 100, moderate; 101 to 200, unhealthy; 201 to 300, very unhealthy and 300 and above, hazardous.
API data is released hourly based on readings from 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide. — Bernama

Title: Kelantan sets sights on petroleum, gas opportunities through new state vehicle
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Aug 12 — The Kelantan government intends to strengthen its involvement in the petroleum and gas industry to ensure that the benefits of natural resources can be enjoyed by the people, besides contributing to the state’s sustainable economic development.
Kelantan Deputy Menteri Besar, Datuk Dr Mohamed Fadzli Hassan said the effort must take into account existing legislation including the Petroleum Development Act 1974 as well as Kelantan’s constitutional position which is different from Sarawak, which has certain rights under the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63).
“In line with the state government’s wishes, the Kelantan Menteri Besar Corporation has established Kelantan Ventures Sdn Bhd (KVSB) as a special purpose company to explore opportunities for participation in the petroleum and gas industry in a more structured and strategic manner.
“Through KVSB, Kelantan is building capacity, exploring investment opportunities and establishing collaborations with reputable companies in the industry value chain,” he said.
He said this when answering a question from Mohamad Nasriff Daud @ Daud Yatimee (PAS-Pengkalan Pasir) regarding the state government’s intention to establish a petroleum and gas corporation at the State Legislative Assembly sitting at Kota Darulnaim Complex here today.
Explaining further, Mohamed Fadzli said the participation would focus on the development of the petroleum and gas value chain including supply bases, logistics and support services for the upstream and downstream sectors, in addition to exploring opportunities in the energy sector.
He said the approach was in line with the development of the Northern Offshore Oil & Gas Corridor which includes the Tok Bali Supply Base (TBSB), Tok Bali Industrial Park (TBIP) as well as integration with the East Coast Rail Link Project logistics network in the future.
“The state government will continue to strengthen institutional capacity and examine appropriate participation models based on existing legal space to ensure that Kelantan’s involvement in the petroleum and gas industry can be strengthened in a phased and responsible manner.
“This step is also to ensure that the returns from the participation can be channeled to the state and subsequently enjoyed by all the people,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Johor housewife charged with murdering 16-month-old step-granddaughter in Kota Tinggi
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Aug 12 — A 39-year-old housewife was charged in the Magistrate’s Court here today with murdering her 16-month-old step-granddaughter last month.
The accused, Nurul Farhana Laily Shah, indicated that she understood the charge after it was read before Magistrate Hafizah Abdul Rajak.
However, no plea was recorded from the accused, who is also the victim’s step-grandmother, as the case falls under the jurisdiction of the High Court.
According to the charge, Nurul Farhana is accused of murdering Nur Anggun Dahlia Abdullah between 12.30pm on July 30 and 9.30am on July 31 at a house along Jalan SS 6/13 in Taman Sri Saujana here.
The charge was framed under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which carries the death penalty or imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years upon conviction. If the death penalty is not imposed, the offender shall also be sentenced to not fewer than 12 strokes of the cane.
The prosecution was conducted by Deputy Public Prosecutor Nor Afiqah Musa, while the accused was represented by counsels Lydiana Mansor and Farah Yasmin.
Bail was not offered to the accused as an offence under Section 302 of the Penal Code is non-bailable.
The court set Dec 11 for mention and submission of the chemical, autopsy and deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) reports.
Yesterday, Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad confirmed that three individuals, including the victim’s step-grandmother, had been detained to assist in the murder investigation following an incident at their home in Taman Sri Saujana.
He was reported as saying that the victim’s step-grandmother had previously lodged a police report on July 31, claiming that her granddaughter had died while sleeping at the house.
However, an autopsy conducted at Pasir Gudang Hospital found that the baby’s cause of death was abdominal and chest trauma caused by blunt force, in addition to several wounds and bruises on her body.

Title: Immigration dept caps Malaysian passport validity at 10 years after overseas travel issues, offers free replacement
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — The Immigration Department has set the maximum validity period of the Malaysian International Passport (PMA) at 10 years with immediate effect, following issues faced by some Malaysian passport holders travelling overseas with passports valid for more than 10 years.
The department said the move was aimed at standardising the implementation of PMA requirements and avoiding confusion during international travel.
As part of the measures, the department will issue notification letters to airlines to assist affected Malaysian travellers overseas.
It will also stop issuing PMAs with validity periods exceeding 10 years until the issue is resolved with the relevant parties.
Existing PMA holders with validity periods exceeding 10 years will be given free replacement passports, with the new passports having a maximum validity of 10 years.
The department said affected PMA holders would also be given priority for passport replacement.
The Immigration Department said it remained committed to improving the implementation of PMA requirements to facilitate matters for Malaysians and ensure smoother international travel.

Title: Sarawak Immigration detains 42 foreigners over suspected immigration offences
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 12 — The Malaysian Immigration Department Sarawak has netted 42 foreigners suspected of committing various immigration offences.
The operations conducted by the Kuching enforcement division, from 10pm on Aug 10 to 3am yesterday, involved checks at three locations comprising shared houses and rented rooms around Jalan Merdang Limau, Kota Samarahan and Mile 6, Jalan Penrissen.
The department said 45 individuals were inspected during Ops Sapu and Ops Kutip, with 42 detained on suspicion of offences under Section 15(1)© of the Immigration Act 1959/63 for unlawful entry and Section 6(1)© of the same Act for overstaying.
The operation followed complaints and intelligence gathered by the Kuching Immigration Enforcement Division to ensure compliance with immigration laws.
Enforcement operations would continue to be intensified based on intelligence and public complaints received, said the department.
It also urged members of the public to provide information on suspected violations of immigration laws to the department. — The Borneo Post

Title: Kota Kinabalu airport security needs a closer look, Sabah rep says after string of overseas drug arrests
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 12 — The relevant agencies have been called on to undertake a comprehensive security audit of Kota Kinabalu International Airport (KKIA).
In making the call, Kapayan assemblyman Chin Teck Ming proposed that the review should include, among others, the adequacy of passenger screening procedures; baggage screening technology and detection capability; intelligence-led passenger risk assessment; as well as random and secondary screening procedures.
Chin suggested the audit should also include staffing levels during operational hours; training and competency of screening personnel; coordination among all enforcement agencies operating at KKIA; and whether additional manpower, equipment, and technology are required to meet the highest international aviation security standards.
He called for the findings to be made public so that Sabahans and all Malaysians can be assured that the international gateway continues to operate at the highest level of security.
According to him, security failures are often recognised only after disaster strikes and urged the government not wait for tragedy before taking action.
“They identify vulnerabilities early, strengthen their systems, and eliminate weaknesses before innocent lives are placed at risk. The recent arrests should therefore be treated as a serious warning,” Chin said, citing the recent series of drug-smuggling cases involving Malaysian travellers arrested upon arrival overseas.
He stressed the need to ensure that every possible weakness is identified and rectified before it can be exploited.
“The travelling public deserves confidence that every reasonable measure has been taken to protect them. When it comes to aviation security, ‘good enough’ is never good enough.
“Airport security is not merely a law enforcement issue. It is a matter of national security.
“Any weakness that can be exploited to smuggle drugs today may equally be exploited tomorrow to transport firearms, explosives or materials capable of facilitating acts of terrorism,” added Chin.
On Monday, New Straits Times reported that a Malaysian arriving from Bangkok was detained for allegedly attempting to smuggle more than 4kg of hydroponic cannabis through Chennai International Airport in India.
On Aug 4, Bernama reported another Malaysian was arrested in Indonesia for allegedly attempting to smuggle nearly 1kg of methamphetamine and more than 1,000 ecstasy pills concealed beneath a corset through Juanda International Airport in East Java after arriving from Kuala Lumpur.
Last month, a Malaysian pilot was arrested in Jakarta for allegedly smuggling in 26kg of MDMA while on the job and under the influence of drugs. — The Borneo Post

Title: Upko leader backs call for Sabah, Sarawak to secure one-third of parliamentary seats
Article:
PENAMPANG, Aug 12 — United Progressive Kinabalu Organisation (Upko) Putatan division chief Jason Lee has backed the party president’s call for Sabah and Sarawak to be allocated no less than one-third of parliamentary seats as a constitutional safeguard.
He said the demand was also in line with the original spirit of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63).
“I support this demand. To me, one-third of the seats is not merely a question of numbers. It is about the strength of our voice and protecting the interests of Sabah and Sarawak within the Federation,” said Jason, who was newly elected to Upko’s Supreme Council at the party’s 17th Triennial Delegates Conference held on Monday at the Kadazan Dusun Cultural Association (KDCA) near here.
“We want to ensure that when matters affecting Sabah are discussed at the federal level, Sabah’s voice is not a small one that can easily be ignored.
“We want Sabah’s voice to carry strength commensurate with Sabah’s position as one of the territories that formed Malaysia,” he said.
However, he stressed that the number of seats alone would not be enough.
“We must also ensure that the representatives given the mandate by the people of Sabah have the courage to speak up for Sabah. They must understand MA63. They must understand Sabah’s rights. And they must have the courage to defend the interests of the people of Sabah,” said Jason.
“We do not merely want more seats. We want greater power to safeguard Sabah’s voice,” he added.
He said the demand was part of efforts to strengthen constitutional safeguards and Sabah’s position within the Federation.
“I believe this struggle must be pursued consistently, not only when an election is approaching,” said Jason.
Currently, Sabah and Sarawak have a combined 56 parliamentary seats out of 222 nationwide, while Peninsular Malaysia holds 166 seats.
The 56 seats held by Sabah and Sarawak account for about 25.2 per cent of the total, falling short of the one-third representation being sought under the MA63 framework.
If the total number of parliamentary seats remains at 222, one-third would amount to 74 seats. This means Sabah and Sarawak would need a combined 74 seats, an increase of 18 from the current 56, to reach the one-third threshold
Upko president Datuk Ewon Benedick said on Monday that, in preparation for the next election, Sabah must put forward a proposal for the redelineation of parliamentary and State Legislative Assembly seats.
“Under the Federal Constitution, a review of electoral boundaries can be conducted every eight years,” he said.
He also pointed out that the current State Legislative Assembly constituencies date back to 2020, while the current parliamentary constituencies date back to 2004, or 22 years ago.
“And it is now time for the number of parliamentary seats in Sabah to be increased, in line with our demand for one-third of the parliamentary seats to be allocated to the territories of Sabah and Sarawak,” said Ewon.
Former Putatan MP Datuk Dr Marcus Makin Mojigoh had also repeatedly raised the issue during his tenure in Parliament. — The Borneo Post

Title: Malaysia and Australia eye domestic neodymium magnet production in rare earth push
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 — Malaysia and Australia are exploring closer cooperation in the rare earth elements (REE) and critical minerals sectors, including the development of domestic neodymium magnet manufacturing.
The Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry (NRES) said the matter was among the key areas discussed during a meeting between Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup and Australian High Commissioner to Malaysia Danielle Heinecke at the Parliament building yesterday.
It said Malaysia recognises Australia’s technical expertise and leadership in the critical minerals sector and is committed to developing a comprehensive domestic REE value chain, from midstream to downstream, in line with the National Mineral Policy 3 (NMP3).
“The discussions also focused on the exchange of best practices in managing rare earth processing residues, particularly neutralisation underflow residue (NUF), as well as efforts to develop domestic neodymium magnet manufacturing capabilities,” it said in a statement.
Apart from critical minerals, the ministry said both sides also discussed hazardous waste management, marine ecosystem conservation, climate financing and Malaysia’s commitment to the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31).
It said the combination of Australia’s technical expertise and Malaysia’s commitment to sustainable resource management is expected to serve as a catalyst for competitive green economic growth while delivering long-term benefits to both countries.
The meeting also aimed to strengthen bilateral ties and explore new areas of cooperation under the framework of the Malaysia-Australia Comprehensive Strategic Partnership (CSP), established in 2021, it added. — Bernama

Title: JPJ to meet RXZ Members organisers over safety, improvements to motorcycle gathering
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — The Road Transport Department (JPJ) will hold its first engagement session with RXZ Members organisers to discuss improvements to the motorcycle gathering, following a series of accidents linked to the event,
Sinar Harian
reported.
JPJ Senior Director of Enforcement Datuk Muhammad Kifli Ma Hassan said the session aimed to hear the organisers’ views and propose several improvements to the programme.
“We are not trying to restrict the event. What is important is road safety, not only for the participants but also for other road users,” he was quoted as saying by the Malay-language daily at a press conference at the JPJ Kuala Lumpur office yesterday.
Muhammad Kifli said the engagement session would be held at the JPJ headquarters in Putrajaya today.
On Aug 2, media reported that JPJ would step up enforcement against participants of motorcycle gatherings, including holding an engagement session with organisers following accidents frequently associated with such events.
JPJ director-general Datuk Aedy Fadly Ramli said the department did not prevent the organisation of motorcycling programmes, but all participants were required to comply with road laws and vehicle technical regulations.
Meanwhile, 46 road accidents involving motorcyclists were recorded over four days from July 30 to Aug 2 during the RXZ Members 8.0 programme.
Bukit Aman Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department director Datuk Seri Muhammed Hasbullah Ali said 11 cases, or 24 per cent, involved fatal accidents, while five cases (11 per cent) involved serious injuries and 30 cases (65 per cent) involved minor injuries.

Title: Legal action looms for Facebook page attacking Perak state developer
Article:
IPOH, Aug 12 — The Perak State Development Corporation (PKNPk) has lodged reports with the police and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) over the dissemination of various allegations against the corporation, its management and certain individuals linked to the organisation.
In a statement, PKNPk said it was aware of several posts by a Facebook page which had recently been continuously publishing various serious allegations against PKNPk and its management.
The corporation said the dissemination of allegations that were not based on verifiable facts could potentially damage the reputation and credibility of PKNPk and related parties, as well as undermine the confidence of investors, stakeholders and the general public.
As a state-owned development agency, PKNPk said it respected the right of any party to voice opinions, provide views and make criticisms through the appropriate channels, but such freedom should not be abused.
“In this regard, PKNPk lodged several reports and complaints with police and MCMC between July 30 and Aug 3 regarding the dissemination of the allegations,” the statement, posted on PKNPk’s official Facebook page, said.
PKNPk also said it had sought legal advice and would take appropriate action to protect the organisation’s interests, reputation and integrity against any party that published or disseminated false or defamatory statements, or statements that violated the law.
“PKNPk will continue to focus on fulfilling its mandate and responsibilities as the state’s development agency, guided by the principles of integrity, accountability and the interests of Perak,” the statement said. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak air quality stays unhealthy in nine areas as transboundary haze persists
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 12 — The air quality in nine areas in Sarawak was at an unhealthy level as at 8 am today due to transboundary haze, compared with 11 areas yesterday morning.
According to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), Serian had an Air Pollutant Index reading of 194, Kuching (172), Samarahan (170), Sarikei (161), Bintulu (157), Sri Aman (157), Samalaju (152), Sibu (151) and Miri (133).
An API reading of 0 to 50 indicates good air quality; 51 to 100, moderate; 101 to 200, unhealthy; 201 to 300, very unhealthy and 300 and above, hazardous.
API data is released hourly based on readings from 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide. — Bernama

Title: Op Chick: MACC busts illegal China frozen chicken import ring in Sabah, three nabbed
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has busted a syndicate suspected of illegally importing frozen chicken from China into Sabah by allegedly bribing authorities at a port,
Sinar Harian
reported.
Citing a source, the Malay daily reported that 10 containers of frozen chicken believed to have been illegally imported from China were seized under Op Chick on Tuesday morning.
The operation was carried out by the MACC’s Intelligence Division in cooperation with the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) and the Royal Malaysian Customs Department.
Preliminary investigations found that the containers had allegedly been falsely declared and did not undergo the required inspection process.
Three men in their 30s to 50s, comprising forwarding agents and a company manager, were also arrested following the operation.
The MACC is reportedly identifying other individuals suspected of involvement in the case.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Sri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the operation and arrests when contacted by Sinar Harian.
He said the three suspects would be brought to the Kota Kinabalu Magistrates’ Court for a remand application to assist investigations.
The case is being investigated under Section 17 of the MACC Act 2009.

Title: Taiwanese YouTuber targeted for foreign cash, 12 nabbed in RM35,000 Cheras robbery
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — Police have arrested 12 Malaysians, including four women, over the alleged assault and robbery of a Taiwanese YouTuber at a condominium in Cheras,
The Star
reported last night.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said police received a report from a Japanese man on Aug 1 over the incident, in which the Taiwanese victim was allegedly assaulted and robbed.
“The victim suffered injuries and losses amounting to about RM35,000,” he was quoted as saying.
Fadil said the suspects were believed to have targeted the victim after learning that he was carrying a large amount of cash in foreign currencies.
“This was believed to have been the initial trigger for the criminal act,” he said.
Following the report, police launched a special operation involving the Cheras district police headquarters’ Criminal Investigation Division and the Kuala Lumpur Criminal Investigation Department.
Fadil said the 12 suspects — eight men and four women aged between 26 and 48 — were arrested in separate operations across Selangor, Negri Sembilan and Kuala Lumpur.
Seven suspects were released on police bail on Aug 7 after having their statements recorded, while the remaining five have been remanded until Aug 13 to assist investigations.
The case is being investigated under Section 170 of the Penal Code for impersonating a public servant and Section 395 for gang robbery.
Police are also tracking down another suspect who remains at large and urged anyone with information to come forward to assist investigations.

Title: Five Penang blackspots in police cross-agency push to clean up crime hotspots
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 12 — Five blackspot areas in Penang have been identified as the focus of the 2026 Penang Police Contingent Whitening The Blackspot United For Safety Crime Prevention Initiative.
State police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said the initiative takes an integrated approach to tackling security, crime, social, infrastructure and environmental issues in the identified areas.
“The initiative adopts a whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach that brings together the police, government agencies, local authorities, elected representatives, communities, non-governmental organisations, the private sector and strategic partners in a coordinated effort.
“It is hoped that the approach will result in more structured, effective and sustainable strategic measures to create a safe, clean, orderly and conducive environment in line with the aspirations of ‘United For Safety’,” he said in a post on the Penang Police Contingent Facebook page yesterday.
He said this during an engagement session on the initiative at Dewan Yayasan Aman in Kubang Semang near here yesterday.
The engagement session provided departments, agencies and strategic partners with an avenue to share views and proposals based on their respective areas of expertise and authority, particularly on action plan coordination, intervention projects, resource needs and collaborative efforts.
Also present at the engagement session were Bagan Dalam assemblyman K. Kumaran, representatives of state assemblymen, heads of government departments and agencies, representatives of local authorities, senior police officers, strategic partners and chairmen of Rukun Tetangga Areas. — Bernama

Title: All registered Malaysians in Colombia safe after 7.4-magnitude quake, says Wisma Putra
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 — The Foreign Ministry has confirmed that all registered Malaysians in Colombia are safe and accounted for following a powerful 7.4-magnitude earthquake that struck western Colombia on Monday.
In a statement issued on Tuesday (Aug 11), the Foreign Ministry, also known as Wisma Putra, said the Embassy of Malaysia in Lima, Peru, which is concurrently accredited to Colombia, remains in close contact with the relevant local authorities and is closely monitoring developments.
It said that the earthquake struck at about 7.34 am local time, with its epicentre located near the town of San José del Palmar in the Department of Chocó.
Tremors were felt across much of Colombia, particularly in the central region, including Cali, Pereira, Manizales, and Armenia, as well as the capital, Bogotá, resulting in significant damage to buildings and infrastructure.
“The Ministry extends its deepest sympathies to the government and people of the Republic of Colombia, especially those affected by this devastating natural disaster,” the statement said.
Wisma Putra added that Colombian authorities are continuing to assess the situation, while the number of casualties and the full extent of the damage have yet to be determined.
It advised Malaysians residing in or travelling to Colombia, particularly those in affected areas, to exercise utmost caution, remain vigilant, and comply with instructions and advisories issued by Colombian authorities and local emergency services.
Malaysians who have yet to register their presence in the country are strongly urged to do so immediately via e-Konsular.
Those requiring immediate consular assistance or with information regarding Malaysians who may be affected can contact the Malaysian Embassy in Lima via telephone or WhatsApp at (511) 422 0297, (511) 441 1939, or (511) 441 0795, or by email at mwlima@kln.gov.my or malawakillima@gmail.com.
Wisma Putra said it will continue to monitor the situation closely and provide updates as necessary. — Bernama

Title: Tabung Haji’s RM10b hole could have been avoided if BNM warnings were heeded, Dewan Rakyat told
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — The financial crisis of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) could have been avoided if the institution had taken appropriate action regarding warning letters concerning TH’s financial position, reserve levels, and liquidity management issued by Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) since 2014.
Minister in the Prime Department (Religious Affairs) Dr. Zulkifli Hasan said that based on records, BNM issued five warning letters to the TH Chairman and the responsible Minister between August 2014 and September 2016.
“Had those warnings been addressed appropriately since 2014, TH’s financial problems likely could have been contained earlier, and the government’s need to bail out TH could have been avoided.
“Instead, TH’s financial position continued to deteriorate until its asset-liability deficit widened to approximately RM10 billion by the end of 2018, requiring a bailout from the government to prevent a larger financial crisis,” he said.
Zulkifli said this when winding up debate at the Special Meeting of the Dewan Rakyat regarding the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) Report concerning TH in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday.
Zulkifli said the matter is supported by the RCI’s view that TH should not have been given a Clean Audit Certificate; instead, the matters stated as “Emphasis of Matter” should have been declared as non-compliance (a qualified opinion).
For information, BNM, in line with its functions relating to financial stability, continuously monitors developments within non-bank financial institutions, including TH.
“Based on the monitoring and discussions conducted, BNM was informed of the steps taken regarding the issues raised by BNM. However, in reality and as proven, TH’s actions starting in 2014 did not show that BNM’s warnings and reminders were given serious attention at all,” he said.
According to him, this also involved the declaration of dividends when assets were less than liabilities – contrary to Section 22 of the Tabung Haji Act – as well as the practice of distributing unprudent hibah (dividends/grants) not guided by the actual financial position, which continued until 2017.
In his winding-up speech, Zulkifli also gave an assurance that amendments to the Tabung Haji Act 1995 (Act 535) will be implemented immediately to complete the governance improvements already carried out.
In addition, he said Forensic Auditing has already been conducted on the investments listed in the RCI report.
“Meanwhile, the proposal to establish a Multi Agency Task Force to investigate each investment at risk of loss is welcomed and will be examined for implementation.
“Overall, the government’s action is clear, which is to investigate, take enforcement action, recover assets, and strengthen laws and governance to ensure the trust and interests of TH depositors continue to be protected,” he said.
Meanwhile, Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul expressed his appreciation to the Members of Parliament who participated in the debate on the RCI report regarding TH, which sat in the Dewan Rakyat for more than 10 hours yesterday.
“Thank you, Yang Berhormat... The Dewan Rakyat has been sitting continuously since 10:00 am, seeing 39 Members of Parliament take part. We have also heard two ministers winding up, namely the Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) and the Second Minister of Finance.
“However, we do not stop here because we still have the Third Meeting taking place in October, and we can continue to ask questions if there are things we feel are unclear today,” he said.
Johari then adjourned the special meeting to a date to be fixed. — Bernama

Title: Heritage pride, yes; public holiday, no: Melaka govt sets the record straight on Aug 21 despite Unesco heritage link
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 12 — There will be no public holiday in Melaka on Aug 21, as the date is not listed in the state’s 2026 Public Holiday Schedule and no occasional holiday has been declared.
State secretary Datuk Salhah Salleh said a clarification had been issued to dispel public confusion over Aug 21 (Friday), which has been linked to Melaka’s Unesco World Heritage recognition.
“All public services, schooling and daily activities will continue as usual on Aug 21.
“However, this is subject to the regulations set by the respective authorities, employers and institutions,” he said in a statement here yesterday.
At the same time, Salleh said the state government remained committed to preserving and promoting Melaka’s historical, cultural and heritage assets recognised as Unesco World Heritage Sites. — Bernama

Title: Finance Ministry: Tabung Haji’s finances are stronger, but taxpayers still bore the RM13b fallout
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — Lembaga Tabung Haji’s (TH) current position is stable and increasingly stronger, following an increase in assets that exceed liabilities, depositors’ savings, and the distribution rate, said the Ministry of Finance (MOF).
Emphasising the government’s full commitment to TH, the ministry said that the total assets of RM98.58 billion exceeded liabilities of RM95.63 billion as of Dec 31, 2025, while depositors’ savings rose from RM75.4 billion in 2018 to RM93.4 billion in 2025.
“The distribution rate increased from 1.25 per cent in 2018 to 3.50 per cent in 2025, totalling RM3.22 billion,” it said.
In a statement yesterday, MOF reiterated that TH depositors’ savings are safe as the government guarantees the entire savings of each depositor under Section 24 of Act 535.
“The people’s haj savings are safe. The institutions that hold these haj aspirations will always be protected, for today’s generation and future generations,” the ministry explained.
Meanwhile, MOF stressed that TH’s losses stemming from financial and investment mismanagement before 2018 have not disappeared.
It said the government bore the bailout costs through public funds and taxpayers.
“(A total of) 9.7 million depositors also bore the burden, receiving a distribution rate as low as 1.25 per cent in 2018 and around three per cent during the recovery year,” it said.
MOF said that the government will not intervene and will not protect anyone; the decision to prosecute rests entirely with the prosecutors.
“For the same reason, the government is committed to ensuring this crisis does not recur.
“In line with the RCI’s recommendations, the government will proceed with amendments to the Tabung Haji Act 1955 (Act 535), among others to introduce Securities Commission oversight of Tabung Haji’s investment activities,” it added.
Earlier, when winding up at yesterday’s special parliamentary sitting, Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said TH’s losses amounted to nearly RM13 billion, comprising RM10.2 billion of losses borne by the government through Urusharta Jamaah Sdn Bhd (UJSB) in 2018, and RM2.6 billion in impairments borne by TH itself. — Bernama

Title: Perak police crack two cases: Armed robbery of Langkap woman, and Teluk Intan fishing shop break-in where one suspect is only 13
Article:
IPOH, Aug 12 — A local man has been arrested for allegedly being involved in an armed robbery involving an elderly woman at a house in Langkap near Teluk Intan.
Hilir Perak District Police chief ACP Chua Kok Lian said police received a report from the 69-year-old local woman, who claimed she had been robbed by an unidentified man.
He said in the incident at about 4 am, the suspect, who was armed with a machete, allegedly snatched a gold bracelet worn by the victim, causing her to sustain injuries, with losses estimated at RM6,000.
“Following the report, further investigations and intelligence led to the arrest of a 32-year-old man at about 2.30 am (yesterday) in Slim River.
“Police also recovered and seized a gold bracelet believed to be linked to the case for further investigation,” he said in a statement last night.
Chua said the suspect was remanded for seven days until Aug 17 to assist and facilitate investigations under Section 394 of the Penal Code for causing hurt while committing a robbery.
Meanwhile, in a separate statement, Chua said two local men suspected of being linked to a break-in at a fishing equipment shop on Jalan Changkat Jong, Teluk Intan, had also been arrested.
He said police received a report from the shop owner after discovering that the premises had been prised open and broken into on July 30, with an inspection revealing that fishing equipment worth about RM8,000 was missing.
“Following the report, police conducted investigations and intelligence operations before arresting two local males aged 13 and 19 in separate raids.
“Further investigations also led police to recover and seize several items believed to be linked to the case for further investigation,” he said, adding that both suspects would be charged under Section 414 of the Penal Code at the Teluk Intan Magistrate’s Court today. — Bernama

Title: No Subang by-election, EC says after Wong Chen quits as MP
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — The Election Commission of Malaysia (EC) has announced that a by-election (PRK) for the Subang parliamentary constituency will not be held following the resignation of its incumbent, Wong Chen, as the Member of Parliament.
EC Chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said this is based on Article 54(1) of the Federal Constitution, as Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Dr. Johari Abdul has informed the EC that there is no need to fill the vacancy.
“No by-election for the P.104 Subang Parliamentary Constituency will be held,” he said in a statement last night.
He added that the EC received notification from Johari via a letter dated today (August 11) regarding the status of the casual vacancy of the Subang parliamentary seat after it was declared vacant under Article 51 of the Federal Constitution.
Earlier, Johari confirmed at the special meeting of the Dewan Rakyat yesterday that he had officially received Wong Chen’s resignation notice yesterday. — Bernama

Title: Tabung Haji’s RM27.5b UJSB sukuk safe, govt will honour guarantee, says Amir Hamzah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — The government always ensures that its debts are repaid, said Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan.
He said government debt instruments such as Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) and Treasury bills, for example, are consistently serviced by the government.
Amir Hamzah was responding to concerns raised by Hassan Abdul Karim (PH-Pasir Gudang) over whether the government would be able to honour its guarantee for sukuk issued by Urusharta Jamaah Sdn Bhd (UJSB).
UJSB, established on Dec 14, 2018, is a special purpose vehicle (SPV) tasked with managing assets transferred from Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH).
Amir Hamzah also explained that the government had restructured TH’s zero-coupon bond sukuk into sukuk with annual profit distributions to meet payment obligations for the RM27.5 billion sukuk issued by UJSB.
“The sukuk issued in 2018 was structured as a zero-coupon bond, meaning the returns were received at the end of the sukuk’s maturity. At the time, the sukuk was issued at RM19.6 billion, but its value upon maturity was RM27 billion. The difference of about RM8 billion represented the returns to TH,” he said during the winding-up session of the Dewan Rakyat’s Special Briefing on the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on TH, presented by Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan on Tuesday.
“With these returns, TH was able to fund its annual hibah payments. The return on the first sukuk was about 4.05 per cent, while Sukuk 2 offered about 4.1 per cent,” he said.
Amir Hamzah said the restructuring meant that the hibah paid was higher, while the returns were also better than what TH would have earned had the funds been invested in government-issued securities. “We want to ensure that the returns to TH are sufficient and better than those provided previously,” he added.
The RCI also recommended that the returns from the zero-coupon bonds be converted into cash payments.
“Therefore, when we restructured Sukuk 1 and Sukuk 2, we converted them from zero-coupon bonds into sukuk that pay annual coupons. The return is 3.86 per cent, higher than the approximately 3.6 per cent return on government securities. For Sukuk 3, Tabung Haji receives returns of about RM440 million annually. That is the return to Tabung Haji,” he said. — Bernama
